metadata.case_name: MO HEE YUK v. GAMMON SKANSKA LTD AND ANOTHER

plaintiff.occupation_after: supporting services assistant (Hospital Authority); temporarily workshop attendant (Haking Wong Institute of Vocational Education)

injuries.description: left brachial plexus (which is a network of nerves) injury after traction injury.
source: left brachial plexus (which is a network of nerves) injury after traction injury.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of multiple nerves at shoulder or upper arm level

injuries.description: head injury resulting in post-concussional syndrome
source: The board also certified his injury as head injury and left brachial plexus injury resulting in numbness of left upper limb headache, dizziness and poor memory and assessed his permanent loss of earning capacity at 3.5%.
Dr Chan also said that the plaintiff had post-concussional syndrome which might produce on/off headache and fair memory.

injuries.description: post-concussional disorder and post-traumatic stress disorder; adjustment disorder with mixed anxiety and depressed mood
source: Dr Choa opined that he was suffering from a post-concussional syndrome with feature of post-traumatic stress disorder.

Dr Chung opined that as a result of the accident, the plaintiff was suffering from post-concussional disorder which is an acquired impairment in cognitive functioning accompanied by neurobehavioural symptoms.
Dr Chen also found that the plaintiff was suffering from post-concussional disorder and post-traumatic stress disorder as a result of the accident.
He estimated degree of permanency of the psychiatric disability was 60%.

manifestations.description: left upper limb weakness and numbness
difficulty in picking up small objects with chopsticks or small objects like pins with his left hand
reduced grip strength of the left hand
impaired smell and taste / partial loss of smell and taste
irritability / temper outbursts / easily irritable / shouting to his son / tendency to fight with people
anxiety when thinking about the accident and when climbing up and down at construction sites or in handling machines
repeatedly experienced the accident via dreaming and flashback
lack of courage to return to work in construction sites (claimed phobia)

treatments_received: A & E Department attendance at Alice Ho Miu-ling Nethersole Hospital
Transfer to Prince of Wales Hospital
Conservative treatment with drugs and physiotherapy (Orthopaedics)
Follow-up in Neurosurgery Division (Prince of Wales Hospital)
Psychiatric clinic treatment (Shatin Hospital; Kwai Chung Hospital)
Admission to Kwai Chung Hospital for one month in December 2004
treatments_future: maintenance and symptomatic psychiatric treatment for post-concussional disorder for three years at $18,000 per year
treatment by a neurologist for physical symptoms of headache and dizziness (judge allowed $10,000)

losses.description: The plaintiffs competitiveness in the labour market was hampered by his mild memory loss, headache and his mild psychiatric problem.

Dr Choa opined that he was suffering from a post-concussional syndrome with feature of post-traumatic stress disorder. Dr Chung opined that as a result of the accident, the plaintiff was suffering from post-concussional disorder which is an acquired impairment in cognitive functioning accompanied by neurobehavioural symptoms. Dr Chen also found that the plaintiff was suffering from post-concussional disorder and post-traumatic stress disorder as a result of the accident. He estimated degree of permanency of the psychiatric disability was 60%.
